canonical_topic: Physical nature and composition of natural gas
definition: Natural gas is a nonrenewable fossil fuel that exists as a colorless, odorless gas mixture at room temperature, used mainly for heating and power generation.
core_idea: Natural gas is mostly methane but can carry varying amounts of ethane, propane, butane, and non-hydrocarbon gases like nitrogen and CO2, so its composition — and therefore its heat content per unit volume — is not fixed.
key_points: Primary component is methane (CH4); commonly present alongside ethane (C2H6), propane (C3H8), and butane (C4H10)
'Dry' gas is nearly pure methane; 'wet' gas carries significant amounts of the heavier hydrocarbons
Can also contain non-hydrocarbon gases such as nitrogen and carbon dioxide
Because composition varies, it is traded in heat-energy units (Btu, Joules) rather than volume units like cubic feet
relationships: Composition variability is the reason gas is priced/traded by energy content rather than volume
trading_implications: Traders must think in energy-content terms (Btu/MMBtu) rather than raw volume when comparing gas across sources of differing composition
caveats: Assuming natural gas is a pure, uniform substance (pure methane) rather than a variable hydrocarbon mixture
